as_read: Mixed: older trials and two pre-2008 meta-analyses favour leaf and flower extract for heart failure symptoms and exercise capacity, but SPICE and HERB CHF were null on their primary outcomes, and no primary-positive mg-dosed trial matches these labels.

studies_to_add.quote: In this study, WS 1442 had no significant effect on the primary endpoint.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: change in 6 min walk distance at 6 months
studies_to_add.quote: Hawthorn provides no symptomatic or functional benefit when given with standard medical therapy to patients with heart failure.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: not named; maximal workload and symptoms pooled
studies_to_add.quote: These results suggest that there is a significant benefit in symptom control and physiologic outcomes from hawthorn extract as an adjunctive treatment for chronic heart failure.

stop_list: Dose fields can't express drops: 12833999 (3 times 30 drops) and 11715631 (3 x 25 drops) stay in regimen text.
SPICE subgroup claim on sudden cardiac death (LVEF of 25% or more) is left out of outcomes because the abstract doesn't say whether it was prespecified.
clinician_items: 18490196: retrospective analysis of HERB CHF reports higher early heart failure progression on WS 1442 (3.9 times, p = 0.035; adjusted 6.4, p = 0.011) and greater risk at LVEF of 35% or less (3.2, p = 0.02); overall progression 46.6% versus 43.3%, p = 0.86.
19789403: significantly more adverse events on hawthorn (p = 0.02), most non-cardiac.
18254076: one trial reported deaths, three on active and one on control, without further detail.
19019730: adverse events comparable; authors call WS 1442 safe with optimal heart failure medication.
12817526: 8 healthy volunteers, no significant change in digoxin pharmacokinetics with WS 1442 450 mg twice daily.
16762125: no herb-drug interaction found in type 2 diabetes patients on medication (79 patients).
stored_rating_note: positive_strong rests on one 2003 meta-analysis of pre-SPICE trials; SPICE (19019730) and HERB CHF (19789403) were null on primary outcomes. The stored applicability text mentions no later trial.
